peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is avian paramyxovirus?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Avian Paramyxoviruses (APMV) are a group of RNA viruses that cause acute respiratory or neurologic disease. There are 12 recognized serotypes of avian paramyxoviruses (APMV-1 to APMV-12). In wildlife, avian paramyxovirus is most typically seen in cormorants and gulls.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What are the three types of Newcastle disease?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: The disease appears in three forms: lentogenic or mild, mesogenic or moderate and velogenic or very virulent, also called exotic Newcastle disease. The lentogenic strains are very widespread, but cause few disease outbreaks.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Newcastle disease - WOAH - World Organisation for Animal Health

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is paramyxovirus type 1 PPMV1?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Pigeon paramyxovirus (PPMV1) is the name of the disease when pigeons are infected with avian paramyxovirus type 1. The virus is present in most countries, spreads rapidly and can cause high rates of pigeon illness and death.
